title: Unsupervised Machine Learning Classification of FRB 20121102A across Distinct Active Episodes: Implications for FRB Emission Physics and Source Environments
summary: Four clusters were identified. Cluster 1 contains nearly all high-energy bursts and has mean energy about an order of magnitude above the other clusters; it has bimodal-like central-frequency/bandwidth distributions and occupies a distinct width–fluence region. Its fraction is 26.9% in 2019 versus 7.7% and 7.8% in 2022 and 2023. The authors suggest a potentially distinct burst population but do not establish a radiation mechanism. Cluster structure was tested across UMAP/HDBSCAN hyperparameter ranges; cluster proportions include 95% Wilson intervals and the pattern is compared with earlier classifications on the 2019 sample. This is internal robustness and cross-study consistency, not independent replication; physical interpretation is explicitly tentative. The possible distinct emission population is tentative; no radiation mechanism is established.
ai_technology: Unsupervised UMAP dimensionality reduction followed by HDBSCAN clustering of width, bandwidth, central frequency, bandwidth ratio, peak flux, fluence, energy and waiting time; it organizes observed bursts into groups rather than predicting labels.
organization: Department of Astronomy, Tsinghua University, Beijing, China
